statement: A count or version claim lives in exactly ONE authoritative machine-readable place (plugin.json, hooks.json, or the agents/commands/skills directories themselves). Every other surface either derives it at read time or omits the number entirely — prose says 'see hooks.json', never restating a literal count (a literal here would itself become a live claim needing maintenance, which is the trap this rule names). A sync-checking CI gate is the LAST resort, kept only where a consumer genuinely needs a second static copy.

When one surface restates a list, table or enumeration owned by another, the restating copy is updated in the SAME change as its authority, or it is replaced by a pointer to that authority — a second copy that drifts silently is the defect, not the drift.
